issue.title: R0022 — Share physical lunar-light eligibility across sky, clouds, stars and optics
issue.body:
# R0022 — Share physical lunar-light eligibility across sky, clouds, stars and optics

Canonical identity: **theislampill/salah_widget R0022**. Baseline `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`. Future implementation only; no source repair or photometric calibration is claimed by publication.

The renderer intentionally keeps an opaque ashen calendar moon every night, including new/below-horizon states. Atmospheric moonlight must remain a separate physical permission. Today a near-new fixture has main moonlight0 while its lunar halo is0.1423. The target is shared physical eligibility across every atmospheric consumer while preserving the excellent textured calendar/PBR disc.

## Existing mechanism and bounded comparison

[atmosphere](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1618) computes `moonUp`, darkness, a near-new phase gate and `moonlight=moonObject*(.35+.65*f)`. Lunar optics later use a separate `.25+.75*f` envelope, bypassing that near-new gate. Local star wash has another fraction/up expression. [renderMoon's atmospheric glow](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1062) has a `.03+.24*f*f` floor independent of physical eligibility. The opaque disc/occluder and PBR phase lighting have different jobs and must not inherit a zero atmosphere scalar.

Detached tests at22:00,2026-09-08, Madinah, moonalt20/H42, thin cloud show:

| Fraction | Baseline physical scalar / halo | Detached control scalar / halo |
|---|---|---|
| 0.01 | 0 /0.142307 | 0 /0 |
| 0.50 | 0.675 /0.345406 | 0.318310 /0.175914 |
| 0.92 | 0.948 /0.519491 | 0.859365 /0.474928 |
| 1.00 | 1 /same full halo | 1 /same full halo |

The control routes optics through the main physical scalar and tries Lambert-sphere phase flux. New-moon ring removal is visibly supported; a thin crescent's broad ring becomes calmer without losing its textured disc. Full moon, below-horizon and equal-viewport daylight negative controls are pixel-identical. The trial **does not fix the local `.mglow` floor**, so it is not a complete implementation of this issue.

A Lambert sphere is an analytical control, not calibrated lunar-regolith photometry. [USGS lunar calibration](https://www.usgs.gov/calval/lunar-calibration) establishes that lunar irradiance depends on phase/geometry; it does not validate this trial's artistic exposure. No new irradiance accuracy claim or mandatory Lambert replacement is selected.

## Invariant and implementation scope

One accepted lunar state defines physical light eligibility. If it is zero because of daylight, below-horizon or the project's existing near-new gate, **all physical lunar illumination, star wash, halo/corona/paraselenae and local atmospheric glow are zero**. Calendar disc visibility/occlusion and PBR surface appearance remain separate. Different optical phenomena may retain their own condition gates and artistic gains when physical light is eligible; this is not a requirement that every layer share the same opacity.

1. Trace all actual lunar state writers and consumers, including `moonSky`, `moonNow`, `projectStars`, atmosphere/paint, CSS variables and `.mglow`. Use the consumed phase/altitude state consistently; do not create another ephemeris or diagnostic-only value.
2. Derive the shared eligibility at a point available to all consumers; stage paint ordering so no prior-frame eligibility leaks. The default real-time renderer skips `projectStars` after initial projection, while that function also writes local moon wash. Updating its formula alone is insufficient: arrange later appearance/eligibility consumption when lunar state changes, independently of whether star positions are intentionally held. Decouple appearance refresh from projection if useful; do not force celestial positional animation as a side effect. Reuse existing state rather than a second clock or broad state framework. Keep the calendar/physical separation explicit in names/comments.
3. Gate each physical consumer, including local glow, through that eligibility while retaining the baseline allowed-state response initially. Carry the reason/consumed value into the existing diagnostic contract, coordinating with R001D.
4. Compare crescent/half/gibbous/full balance after the gating fix. A phase-response refinement is optional and requires matched crops demonstrating better scene agreement without loss of moon presence, cloud structure or star character. Preserve the baseline curve if no candidate earns adoption; do not expand this issue into an empirical lunar-calibration project.
5. Update DESIGN/OPTICS/HANDOFF and high-value comments affected by physical-light versus calendar semantics. Keep no-build/static architecture and existing lunar texture provenance.

Do not flatten the PBR moon into a sprite, rotate maria with parallactic angle, remove the new-moon slot, change the upright mostly-on-card composition, paint dawn effects, add generic glow or rewrite sky colour globally. Physical eligibility must not make the calendar moon transparent.

## Reproduction and verification

Use a disposable source copy, pinned2026-09-08 Asia/Riyadh at22:00, lat24.47/lon39.61, seed1, accepted synthetic weather: code2, cloud30, low0/mid8/high28%, precip0, temp24°C, RH55%, dew15°C, visibility20km, wind3m/s from225°, gust5. Inject this complete finite record after ordinary fixture readiness and reset initial cloud coverage so a frozen clock cannot retain an earlier scene. Use moon fractions0.01,0.08,0.5,0.92,1, waxing/waning where relevant, altitude20°, H42°. The existing simulation flags supply phase/altitude; test-only injection supplies exact weather layers.

Pin synthetic prayer responses for the fixture date/next day: Fajr04:46/04:47, Sunrise06:05, Dhuhr12:19, Asr15:48, Maghrib/Sunset18:33, Isha20:03, timezoneAsia/Riyadh. No field/prayer accuracy is implied. A new document per boot-flag change is required. Wait for actual fonts and PBR texture readiness; freeze settled CSS animation at the same phase for stills. Card325×530, recorded viewport/DPR. Include a byte-identical no-op comparison.

Check near-new, below-horizon(-10°), daylight12:30 and normal above-horizon phases. For eligible phases compare clear, thin high cloud, droplet-cloud corona conditions and overcast so condition gates remain distinct. Record actual consumed eligibility and each physical layer opacity, plus pixels. Keep disc interior/edge crops proving no stars through the moon and no black dark-limb cutout. Use a star-positive control outside the disc; a starless scene cannot prove occlusion.

Acceptance:

- Ineligible physical states produce zero contributions from all enumerated physical consumers, including `.mglow`, while every normal night retains the opaque textured calendar disc.
- Eligible full/half/gibbous/crescent states preserve readable phase, upright maria, lunar source position and differentiated/gated corona/halo/paraselenae. Any deliberately changed phase curve has independent matched visual evidence and honest approximation notes.
- Daylight and below-horizon negative controls show no new scene lighting; no branch makes calendar opacity depend on physical light permission.
- Real elapsed15–60s cloud drift/star glints remain visible where allowed; reduced-motion/full override use fresh documents and actual pixel/clip evidence, never cloud hash.
- Header/footer/prayer stack, sun/solar optics and weather truth are unaffected. No new per-frame texture allocation, canvas readback, second animation loop or network work is introduced; compare warmed paint cost on the same scene.

The investigation's one-desktop comparisons do not certify every browser, DPR or full opacity matrix. Future implementation must supply its own exact-candidate crops and regression evidence. Numeric zero alone cannot pass if the calendar disc vanishes or the scene looks worse.

## Ownership and rollback

[R001D](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/29) owns truthful consumed moon diagnostics, not these art/lighting writers. [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9) owns calendar truth, not lunar irradiance. [R0008](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/8)/[R0020](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/32) own clock contracts. [R0021](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/33) owns first visible initialization and moon/star twilight reveal/occlusion; its geometry/visibility change and this physical-light state/consumer change are distinct but share paint/renderMoon/CSS integration. Serialize those writers and review their combined first-frame eligibility and twilight opacity. No hard semantic dependency requires an ephemeris or calendar rewrite.

Rollback the shared-light patch if any phase becomes transparent/blank, new moon emits physical light, optics become generic/detached, or steady motion/cost worsens materially. Roll back only an optional phase curve if that refinement loses the comparison; do not restore the zero-eligibility leak to preserve an unqualified aesthetic. Done requires complete consumer enumeration, exact integrated before/after crops and the preserved calendar/physical distinction.
